এস,আর,ও নং- ১৭৪-আইন/২০১৬/৩৬/কাস্টমস।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 219(1), THIRD SCHEDULE এর item 21 এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড, নিম্নরূপ বিধিমালা প্রণয়ন করিল, যথা :-

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered under the Customs Act 1969 to formulate and issue customs-related rules.
Customs Act 1969: The Act serves as the foundational legal authority under which the National Board of Revenue exercises its rule-making power. Specifically, Section 219(1) of the Act is invoked in conjunction with the Third Schedule to authorize the issuance of new customs regulations.
Third Schedule: The Third Schedule is referenced in conjunction with Section 219(1) of the Customs Act 1969 to provide the legal basis for the current regulatory notification.
S.R.O. 174-AIN/2016: This Statutory Regulatory Order is issued by the National Board of Revenue to enact new rules under the authority granted by the Customs Act 1969.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ১। সংক্ষিপ্ত শিরোনাম।— এই বিধিমালা কাস্টমস এজেন্ট লাইসেন্সিং বিধিমালা, ২০১৬ নামে অভিহিত হইবে।

Customs Agent Licensing Rules 2016: The current legal instrument is officially titled the Customs Agent Licensing Rules 2016.

Customs Act 1969: This law is defined as the Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) for the purposes of these rules.
Customs Agent: A Customs Agent is defined as a person or institution performing tasks related to the import or export of goods or baggage, or the entry or exit of vehicles at a customs station, as per the objectives of section 207 of the Customs Act.
Customs Government: This term refers to the customs authority or official appointed under rule 17 of these regulations.
Customs Station: This refers to the definition of a customs station as specified in section 2(k) of the Customs Act.
Custom House: This refers to a custom house declared according to section 9(e) of the Customs Act.
Company: This refers to a company as defined in section 2(d) of the Companies Act, 1994.
Customer: This refers to a person or institution that imports goods from abroad or exports goods to a foreign country.
Form: This refers to the forms annexed to these rules for official use.
Firm: This refers to a firm as defined in section 4 of the Partnership Act, 1932.
National Board of Revenue: The term Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue, as specified in section 2(e) of the Customs Act.
Reference License: This refers to a license granted under the provisions of rule 11 of these regulations.
License: This refers to a license granted under rule 5 which authorizes an entity to function as a Customs Agent.
Licensing Authority: This refers to the authority constituted under rule 3 for the purposes of managing and issuing customs agent licenses.

৩। লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ।— (১) লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ কাস্টমস এজেন্ট লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিবে।

(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এর উদ্দেশ্যপূরণকল্পে নিম্নবর্ণিত কর্মকর্তাগণের সমন্বয়ে লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ গঠিত হইবে, যথা:-
(ক) কাস্টম হাউসে কর্মরত একজন অতিরিক্ত কমিশনার এবং একজন ডেপুটি কমিশনার; অথবা
(খ) কাস্টম হাউসে অতিরিক্ত কমিশনার না থাকিলে একজন যুগ্ম কমিশনার এবং একজন সহকারী কমিশনার।

(৩) উপ-বিধি (২) এর দফা (ক) এর ক্ষেত্রে অতিরিক্ত কমিশনার সভাপতি ও ডেপুটি কমিশনার সদস্য-সচিব হইবেন এবং দফা (খ) এর ক্ষেত্রে যুগ্ম-কমিশনার সভাপতি এবং সহকারী কমিশনার সদস্য-সচিব হইবেন।

Customs Agent License: The Licensing Authority is responsible for granting licenses to customs agents.
Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority is formally constituted by specific customs officials designated to oversee the issuance of customs agent licenses.
The composition of the authority depends on the availability of specific senior ranking officers at the custom house, with defined roles for chairperson and member-secretary.
Commissioner of Customs: The roles within the Licensing Authority are filled by officials such as the Additional Commissioner, Joint Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or Assistant Commissioner, depending on the available staffing levels at the custom house.

৪। লাইসেন্স প্রদানে বোর্ডের পূর্বানুমতি।— (১) লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিবার পূর্বে সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশনের বিদ্যমান লাইসেন্স সংখ্যা, বিগত ৫ (পাঁচ) বৎসরের আমদানি-রপ্তানির পরিসংখ্যান এবং নূতন লাইসেন্স প্রদানের যৌক্তিকতা উল্লেখপূর্বক অনুমতি গ্রহণের জন্য বোর্ডে লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিবে।

(২) বোর্ড উপ-বিধি (১) এর অধীন আবেদন প্রাপ্তির পর উহা যাচাই-বাছাইপূর্বক লাইসেন্স প্রদানের যৌক্তিকতা বিবেচনা করিয়া সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টম হাউসকে লাইসেন্স প্রদানের অনুমতি প্রদান করিবে।

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the authority responsible for granting prior approval for the issuance of new licenses.
Upon receiving a written application, the Board evaluates the necessity of new licenses based on existing license counts and recent trade statistics before granting permission to the customs house.
Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority must submit a formal written application to the National Board of Revenue before issuing any new licenses.
This application must include justification for the new license, the current number of active licenses at the customs station, and trade statistics from the previous five years.
Customs House: The Customs House receives the authority to grant new licenses only after the National Board of Revenue has reviewed the application and provided formal permission.

Customs Agent License: The licensing authority invites applications for customs agent licenses by issuing public notices in newspapers and on notice boards following board approval.
Applicants must submit a detailed application containing personal identification, financial solvency documents, academic qualifications, and evidence of professional experience or trade standing.

Upon preliminary acceptance of the application and successful completion of a written examination, the applicant must provide specific fees, security deposits in the form of savings certificates, and bonds to be issued the license.
The licensing authority must grant the license within a specified timeframe after verifying all documentation, with provisions for the board to extend this period if necessary.
National Board of Revenue: The board provides the necessary authorization for the licensing authority to initiate the customs agent license application process.
The licensing authority may request the board for an extension of time if it fails to grant the license within the prescribed regulatory period.
Customs Act 1969: Applicants are required to demonstrate practical experience and knowledge concerning the Customs Act 1969, Value Added Tax laws, and import-export policies as part of their eligibility for a customs agent license.

processed_clauses.clause_title: নিজস্ব পণ্য খালাসের (Self Clearance) জন্য লাইসেন্স প্রদান
processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৬। নিজস্ব পণ্য খালাসের (Self Clearance) জন্য লাইসেন্স প্রদান।— কোন ব্যক্তি তদ্কর্তৃক আমদানিকৃত বা রপ্তানিযোগ্য পণ্য নিজস্ব প্রতিষ্ঠানের মাধ্যমে খালাস করিবার জন্য এই বিধিমালার অধীন লাইসেন্স প্রাপ্তির সকল শর্ত পূরণপূর্বক আবেদন করিলে লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ যাচাই-বাছাইপূর্বক বিধি ৫ অনুসারে শুধুমাত্র নিজস্ব প্রতিষ্ঠানের পণ্য খালাসের জন্য ফরম 'খ' অনুযায়ী আবেদনকারীকে লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিবে।

Customs Clearance: This clause establishes a process for entities to obtain a license for self-clearance of their imported or export-ready goods. The license allows businesses to manage their own customs clearance procedures directly instead of relying solely on external clearing agents, provided they meet all stipulated regulatory conditions.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for reviewing and verifying applications submitted by businesses seeking a license for self-clearance. Upon satisfying the necessary criteria and documentation, the authority is empowered to grant the license using the prescribed official format.
Self-Clearance License: A self-clearance license is granted to applicants who fulfill all legal requirements, enabling them to process the customs clearance of their own company's goods. The license is restricted to the licensee's own goods and is issued in accordance with the application process specified in the relevant rules.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৭। লাইসেন্সের মেয়াদ।— এই বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত লাইসেন্সের মেয়াদ হইবে লাইসেন্স প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে পরবর্তী ৫ (পাঁচ) বৎসর।

Customs License: A license granted under these rules is valid for a period of five years from the date of its issuance.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
৮। লাইসেন্স প্রদানের ক্ষেত্রে বিধি-নিষেধ।— এই বিধিমালার অন্যান্য বিধিতে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, সম্পূর্ণ বিদেশী মালিকানাধীন কোন প্রতিষ্ঠানকে এই বিধিমালার আওতায় লাইসেন্স প্রদান করা যাইবে না :

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, দেশী ও বিদেশী যৌথ মালিকানায় প্রতিষ্ঠিত কোম্পানি লাইসেন্স পাইবার যোগ্য হইবে, যদি বিদেশী মালিক বা মালিকদের শেয়ার ধারণের পরিমাণ উক্ত কোম্পানির মোট শেয়ারের শতকরা ৪০ (চল্লিশ) এর অধিক না হয়।

Customs License: This clause imposes restrictions on the issuance of licenses under these rules.
Entities that are entirely foreign-owned are ineligible to be granted a license under this regulatory framework.
Joint Venture Company: Companies established with joint domestic and foreign ownership are eligible to obtain a license.
Eligibility is subject to the condition that the total shareholding of foreign owners does not exceed a specified percentage of the company's total shares.

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent must apply for license renewal at least forty-five working days before the expiration of their current license.

The agent is required to submit specific documentation, including copies of their original license, trade license, income tax certificate, and proof of association membership, along with payment of renewal fees.

Renewal may be denied if the agent's performance is unsatisfactory, if they are involved in illegal activities under the Customs Act 1969, or if there are outstanding government dues or customs-related cases against them.
Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority is responsible for processing renewal applications and may grant a time extension of up to thirty days in two installments if the agent fails to apply within the specified period.
The authority must review the submitted documents and the agent's past performance before deciding to renew the license for a five-year term.
The Licensing Authority must provide written notification to the Customs Agent within twenty working days if it decides to reject a renewal application based on specified grounds.
Customs Act 1969: This Act serves as the legal framework under which a Customs Agent's activities are monitored for compliance during the license renewal process.
Serious violations or involvement in illegal clearance activities prohibited under this Act constitute grounds for the refusal of a license renewal.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Compliance with this Act regarding taxation procedures is a mandatory criterion that a Customs Agent must demonstrate to qualify for license renewal.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ১০। লাইসেন্সের অধিক্ষেত্র।— এই বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত লাইসেন্সের অধিক্ষেত্র হইবে লাইসেন্সে উল্লিখিত সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস বন্দর, কাস্টম হাউস বা কাস্টমস স্টেশন।

Customs License: The jurisdiction of a license issued under these rules is specifically defined as the customs port, custom house, or customs station mentioned in the license document itself.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
১১। রেফারেন্স লাইসেন্স।— কোন কাস্টমস এজেন্ট মূল লাইসেন্সে উল্লিখিত কাস্টমস স্টেশন ব্যতীত অন্য কোন কাস্টমস স্টেশনের রেফারেন্স লাইসেন্স প্রাপ্তির জন্য মূল লাইসেন্সের কপি এবং বিধি ৫ এ বর্ণিত দলিলাদিসহ ফরম-গ অনুযায়ী আবেদন করিতে পারিবে এবং লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ উক্ত দলিলাদি যাচাই-বাছাইপূর্বক আবেদনকারীর মৌখিক পরীক্ষা গ্রহণের মাধ্যমে রেফারেন্স লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিতে পারিবে :

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, কাস্টমস এজেন্ট এর ন্যূনতম ১০ (দশ) বৎসরের সন্তোষজনক কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করিবার অভিজ্ঞতা থাকিলে বিধি ৫ এর দফা (২) এর উপ-দফা (৭) প্রযোজ্য হইবে না।

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent may apply for a reference license to operate at a customs station other than the one specified in their original license.
To obtain a reference license, the agent must submit a copy of their original license and required documentation to the licensing authority.
Customs Agents with at least ten years of satisfactory operational experience are exempted from specific documentary requirements related to license applications.
Reference License: A reference license allows a Customs Agent to operate at an additional customs station beyond the scope of their original license.
The issuance of a reference license is subject to the verification of submitted documentation and the successful completion of an oral examination conducted by the licensing authority.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for verifying applications for reference licenses, conducting oral examinations for applicants, and ultimately granting the licenses.

১২। লাইসেন্সের অনুলিপি প্রদান।— (১) লাইসেন্স হারাইয়া গেলে বা যে কোন প্রকারে নষ্ট হইয়া গেলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস এজেন্ট ২,৫০০/- (দুই হাজার পাঁচশত) টাকা ফি পরিশোধপূর্বক লিখিত আবেদন করিলে লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ লাইসেন্সের একটি অবিকল নকল প্রদান করিবে।

(২) এই বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত লাইসেন্স হারাইয়া গেলে সংশ্লিষ্ট থানায় সাধারণ ডায়েরী করিতে হইবে এবং উহার একটি অনুলিপি আবেদনের সহিত দাখিল করিতে হইবে।

Customs Agent: A customs agent is entitled to obtain a duplicate copy of their license if the original is lost or damaged upon submission of a written application and payment of the prescribed fee.
The customs agent is required to file a formal police report regarding the loss of their license and must submit a copy of this report along with their application for a duplicate.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is empowered to issue a duplicate license to a customs agent once the mandatory fee is paid and the required procedural conditions, such as filing a police report, are satisfied.

processed_clauses.clause_title: লাইসেন্সের গঠনগত পরিবর্তন বা হস্তান্তরের ক্ষেত্রে বিধি-নিষেধ

Customs Agent License: The license is generally non-transferable and subject to structural change restrictions.

Structural changes to a license are only permitted through conversion into a partnership firm under the Partnership Act, 1932 or a company under the Companies Act, 1994, subject to approval from the licensing authority.
In the event of a licensee's death, the license may be transferred to a legal heir, provided the licensing authority is notified and a formal application is submitted within a specified timeframe.
If a legal heir fails to notify the authority or apply for the transfer within the prescribed period following the licensee's death, the license shall be considered cancelled.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is empowered to approve the structural conversion of a license and to oversee the transfer of a license to a legal heir.
The authority must conduct a qualification examination for partners or directors involved in a structural conversion and for legal heirs seeking license transfer.
Partnership Act 1932: This Act serves as the legal framework under which a licensed customs agency may undergo a structural change by converting into a partnership firm.
Companies Act 1994: This Act serves as the legal framework under which a licensed customs agency may undergo a structural change by converting into a company.

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent is required to perform various professional duties, including representing clients, verifying documents, and ensuring regulatory compliance during import and export processes.

The agent must ensure that all funds received from clients for government dues are deposited promptly into the public treasury and that funds received from the government on behalf of clients are paid to them without delay.
Customs Agents are prohibited from exerting undue influence on customs officials, borrowing money from customs staff, or acting as a guarantor for loans taken by such officials.

The agent must maintain all records, financial documents, bills, and correspondence related to licensing for a minimum period of three years in their office and present them to the customs authority upon request.

Agents are responsible for providing accurate information to clients, notifying customs authorities of any discovered false documentation, and cooperating fully with the customs authorities in the execution of their duties.
Bill of Entry: A Bill of Entry must be submitted electronically or manually, along with appropriate valuation forms, by the Customs Agent after verifying all relevant import documents.
Bill of Export: A Bill of Export must be submitted by the Customs Agent to the customs authority, ensuring that the process remains transparent and that the document is not held in the agent's possession after the customs procedure is completed.
Valuation Rules 2000: Customs Agents must ensure that all declarations for the determination of imported goods' value are prepared and submitted in accordance with the provisions of these rules.
Customs Station: Customs Agents are prohibited from collecting any data or records belonging to the customs authority at a customs station without receiving prior permission from the relevant authorities.
Customs Licensing Authority: The Customs Agent must notify the licensing authority in writing immediately upon any change of their business address.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ১৫। স্বাক্ষর প্রদানের ক্ষমতা।— লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষের অনুমোদনক্রমে কাস্টমস এজেন্ট তাহার পক্ষে কাস্টমস সংক্রান্ত দলিলপত্রে স্বাক্ষর করিবার জন্য এক বা একাধিক ব্যক্তিকে ফরম-ছ এর নমুনা অনুযায়ী দলিল স্বাক্ষরের ক্ষমতা অর্পণ করিতে পারিবেন।

Customs Agent: A customs agent is permitted to delegate the authority to sign customs-related documents to one or more individuals.
